canonical_statement: For every natural number n and every n by n complex matrix A, there is a unitary matrix U such that star U times A times U is upper triangular.

source_root.selection: finite complex matrix specialization of Axler's upper-triangular operator/orthonormal-basis Schur theorem
source_root.citation: Sheldon Axler, Linear Algebra Done Right, fourth edition, Section 6B, Theorem 6.38, printed page 204, with upper-triangular definition on page 203
source_root.review_boundary: The author-hosted PDF was inspected but remains mutable; pinpoint definition transport, immutable preservation/recovery, correction review, source-to-catalog identity, and independent H0 review remain open.

        (@id.{1} (Fin n)))

domain_and_universes: n is an explicit natural number; A is an explicit Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Complex; Fin supplies the canonical finite linear order and decidable equality; the result is Prop.
ordered_binders: A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Complex (explicit universal)
U : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Complex (existential witness)
hypotheses: A is a finite square matrix over Complex
U is required in the conclusion to belong to Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n) Complex
conclusion: There exists U with U in Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin n) Complex and Matrix.BlockTriangular (star U * A * U) id.
minimal_import_basis: Complex.Basic supplies Complex, Matrix.Block supplies Matrix.BlockTriangular, and UnitaryGroup supplies Matrix.unitaryGroup. Deleting each import independently fails elaboration. No eigenvalue, Gram-Schmidt, triangularizable-endomorphism, spectral, or proof-bearing Schur module is imported.
uncredited_alternate_encodings: a separately quantified triangular T with star U * A * U = T
the equivalent reconstruction A = U * T * star U
the operator/orthonormal-basis formulation in Axler Theorem 6.38
